newsitem.title: POLAND: Mostostal Z sees no impact of halted deal.
newsitem.headline: Mostostal Z sees no impact of halted deal.

text.p: Polish construction firm Mostostal Zabrze SA sees its earnings unaffected by a court decision to halt its contract to build the world's tallest TV and radio mast, the firm's deputy chief said.
Ryszard Deren told a news conference on Friday that the company upheld its earlier net profit forecast for 1996 of nine million zlotys.
Mostostal last year won the contract to build the 646-metre mast near Gabin, central Poland, replacing one that collapsed in 1991, and said it had beaten off several European firms to get the job.
But local residents fought the scheme, arguing that the electromagnetic waves from the mast could harm their health.
The court ruled earlier this month that the project infringed new building regulations and had not been properly prepared.
"A halt to the work on the construction of the mast in Gabin will not affect our profits," Deren said.

Poland's Supreme Administrative Court has halted, for environmental reasons, plans by state-owned telecommunications firm TPSA to build the 24-million zloty mast -- a contract won last year by Mostostal.
Deren said TPSA had already paid Mostostal three million zlotys for the work done so far and both companies would meet soon to discuss the future of the project.
